questions.question: Explain what a cleat is for and why it is classed as a mechanical control system.
questions.expected_answer: A cleat is a fitting fixed to a deck, post or wall that holds a rope under tension by friction and jamming, so that increasing load tightens the grip, and that releases the rope instantly without untying a knot. It is a control system because it supplies and multiplies no force; the load in the rope comes from the boat, flag or line, and the cleat governs only whether the rope may move, holding it at a fixed length until the operator releases it, in the same way a ratchet governs the direction a wheel may turn and a brake governs whether it may turn.

questions.question: Describe how a horn cleat, a cam cleat and a jam cleat each hold and release a rope.
questions.expected_answer: A horn cleat is a bar with two projecting horns; a round turn at the base and two or three figure-of-eight turns over the horns hold the rope by friction at each bend, and lifting the turns off releases it. A cam cleat has two spring-loaded toothed cams; the rope pulled down into the gap passes freely inward, and when it tries to run back the teeth grip and the cams swing to pinch harder; lifting the rope up and out releases it. A jam cleat has a tapered slot; the rope pulled toward the narrow end wedges, and a flick back toward the wide end frees it.

questions.question: Evaluate a cleat for a mooring line on a pontoon under fitness for purpose, safety and ergonomics, and describe one way to compare cleats by investigation.
questions.expected_answer: Fitness for purpose: it must hold the mooring load without slipping, with the rope diameter used, wet or dry, so a horn cleat sized for the rope and bolted through with a backing plate is suitable. Safety: it must not release accidentally, which could set the boat adrift, and must release without trapping fingers under load. Ergonomics: it must be workable with one cold hand and placed where the rope leads naturally. An investigation fixes horn, cam and jam cleats to a plank, loads a rope through a pulley with a sand bucket, and records wraps or rope size needed to hold, time to release and slipping when wet, then recommends a cleat for a stated use.
